headline: Selling returned Wed Sep 16: KSE-100 closed DOWN 0.81% at 168,021.80 (-1,370.52pts), giving back most of Tuesday's rally as FFC/NBP/ENGROH/HBL/LUCK led the drags and global bond yields + oil paused ahead of the Fed decision. Regional risk backdrop is unchanged from yesterday, not worse: Brent/WTI still elevated (~$107.8 / ~$104.6) on the Saudi pipeline shutdown and repeated Houthi attacks, and a Saudi claim of a Houthi drone targeting Mecca surfaced today, but Pakistan itself has stated (Sep 10) it is not considering military action under the new Mecca defence pact — no fresh Pakistan-specific escalation. HOUSEKEEPING: today's git pull succeeded — the 'git blocked for 6 straight reviews' issue from recent notes was actually local unpushed commits (advice reviews Sep 9-15) diverging from remote commits (price updates + a Sep 9-10 advice push made via GitHub API), which produced a merge conflict on data/advice.json. market: KSE-100: Wednesday Sep 16 closed at 168,021.80, DOWN 1,370.52pts (-0.81%) — day range 167,849.70 to 169,382.01 — giving back most of Tuesday's +1,421.67pt rally. FFC, NBP, ENGROH, HBL and LUCK were the biggest drags, together weighing the index down by ~706pts; globally, Asian stocks were tentative as bond yields and oil prices paused ahead of the Fed's policy decision. Regional security backdrop: Brent crude ~$107.8/bbl and WTI ~$104.6/bbl, both near four-month highs, on continued disruption from Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline shutdown (blamed on a pro-Iran Iraqi militia, ~4mbpd at risk) and repeated Houthi attacks; Hormuz Strait transit volumes have actually risen to ~12mbpd (7-day avg), suggesting the strait itself remains open despite the rhetoric. A fresh Saudi claim today that a Houthi drone targeted Mecca is a notable headline but not a new category of risk — the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement (Turkiye-Saudi-Pakistan, signed Aug 7, NATO-Article-5-style) has already been tested by earlier Houthi strikes, and Pakistan's foreign ministry stated on Sep 10 it is not considering military action under the pact, prioritizing its balance with Iran. No new Pakistan-specific escalation this review. Drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) is now ~11.4% (168,021.80 close), continuing to widen gradually from the ~10.6% of recent reviews — still past the 10% dry-powder trigger, still short of the 15% heavier-shift threshold. AVN: no new company news since the Sep 2 H1 FY26 loss filing; EXIT call remains unexecuted across many consecutive reviews. EFERT: no new Q3 results or dividend announcement since the already-covered Sep 3 payment (Aug 10 ex-date). No new DRAP pharma-pricing development since yesterday's nuance (still unresolved, still opposed by industry) — no change to the GLAXO/SEARL WATCH stance. DATA QUALITY: stock prices from prices.json updated 2026-09-16T14:11:24Z (~14:11 PKT, current). Fund NAVs remain frozen at Aug 13 — now 34 days stale; this is a separate GitHub-Actions/MUFAP-scraper issue, unrelated to today's resolved git-access confusion, and still unresolved.

entries.basis: Monthly-timeframe accumulation zones for a 10-25yr horizon: where fundamentals + monthly support align to add in small portions. 'entry' = start nibbling at/below; 'add' = deeper monthly support to load more. Pakistan macro-aware (SBP 11.5%, KSE-100 off the Jan ATH). These are accumulation guides, not precise buy/sell signals — verify with your broker.
